title: Sea turtles on the beach
text:
Sea turtles spend almost all of their lives in the sea. They have flat flippers that help them swim, and a hard shell on their backs to keep them safe.

Where do turtles lay eggs?

A mother turtle comes out of the sea at night. She crawls up the sand and digs a hole with her back flippers. She lays about a hundred eggs in the hole. Then she covers them with sand and goes back to the sea. She does not stay to look after them.

Baby turtles

After about two months, the eggs hatch. The baby turtles dig their way out of the sand. They are very small, about the size of a biscuit. They hurry down the beach to the sea. This is a dangerous journey because birds and crabs like to eat them.

Helping turtles

In many places, people look after turtle eggs. They put the eggs in a safe place and let the babies go free when they hatch. Some beaches in Indonesia have turtle centres where children can watch baby turtles swim away.

Did you know?

A sea turtle must come up to the top of the water to breathe air, even though it lives in the sea.
